title: How to group elements in Canva on Mac: step by step, with Command+G
metaTitle: How to Group Elements in Canva on Mac (Step by Step)
description: Learn how to group elements in Canva on Mac with Command+G, the floating toolbar or right-click, plus ungrouping and fixes for a greyed-out Group button.
targetKeyword: how to group elements in canva on mac
secondaryKeywords: ungroup elements in canva on mac
intro: To group elements in Canva on Mac, select two or more elements with Shift-click or a drag box, then press Command+G or right-click the selection and choose Group. To ungroup, press Shift+Command+G, or choose Ungroup from the floating toolbar or the right-click menu.
tldr: Select two or more elements with Shift-click or a drag box.
Press Command+G to group, or right-click the selection and choose Group.
Press Shift+Command+G to ungroup, or use Ungroup in the floating toolbar or right-click menu.
Double-click an element inside a group to edit it without ungrouping.
If Group is greyed out, select at least two elements and turn off the lock on any locked one.

blocks.text: What grouping does in Canva

Grouping ties two or more elements together so you can select them as one set. A headline, a photo and a shape can move as a unit. You do not have to pick each one. That saves time on any layout where parts should stay together.

Grouping is not the same as locking. Lock is a separate button on the floating toolbar. Duplicate makes a copy of your selection. Grouping only links the elements until you break the link with Ungroup.
Select the elements you want to group

Canva needs at least two selected elements before it can group anything. Two methods work well. Shift-click adds each element one click at a time. A drag box selects everything inside the rectangle you draw on an empty part of the canvas.

A drag box also catches things you did not mean to select. A faint background shape or a small icon can slip in. Zoom out so the whole design fits on screen, then draw the box. Check the selection outline before you press a key.

items: Every element you want is highlighted.
No element you want to leave out sits inside the box.
All the selected elements are on the same page.
None of the selected elements is locked.

blocks.text: Group with the floating toolbar

With two or more elements selected, a floating toolbar appears near the selection. In Canva's browser version, the toolbar shows a Group button next to Canva AI tools, Duplicate, Lock, Delete and More. Click Group and the elements become one group.

If you do not see the Group button, check the selection first. A single element cannot form a group. Select a second element and look again. If a text box is still in edit mode, click outside it first. Third-party guides say that can stop grouping.
Group with Command+G
The fastest route is the keyboard. Select your elements, then press Command+G. The Command key carries the ⌘ symbol. Apple's keyboard legend lists ⌘ as Command, ⇧ as Shift and ⌥ as Option.
Do not press Ctrl+G on a Mac. A Supademo guide calls Command+G the Mac version and Ctrl+G the Windows version. Jennifer Maker's cheat sheet lists the same split for group and ungroup.
Group from the right-click menu

Right-click one of the selected elements, then choose Group from the menu. Right-click a grouped element later when you want to ungroup. MakeUseOf describes this route for the browser version. Check the menu wording on your screen, because the desktop app may differ.

blocks.text: Edit an element inside a group

You do not need to ungroup to change one part. Double-click the element inside the group, and it opens for editing. You can change text or swap an image without breaking the group. The element stays in the group afterward.
Say the date line sits in a group on a flyer. A few weeks later the date changes. Double-click the date, type the new one, then click outside the text to finish.
Ungroup elements on a Mac

To ungroup, select the group and press Shift+Command+G. In the browser version you can also select an element in the group and choose Ungroup from the floating toolbar. Right-clicking the group and choosing Ungroup works too.
Ungrouping only breaks the link between the elements. It does not delete them. Group the same elements again with Command+G once the layout settles.
How grouping handles layers and stacking order
Canva stacks elements in layers. Elements higher in the stack sit over the ones below. Grouping elements that sit on different layers groups those layers together, and grouping can reorder them.
Check the layout right after you group. A photo that used to sit under a text box may end up above it. Fix the order before you move on.
When grouping helps and when it gets in the way
Group things that should move together. A headline and its subhead are a good pair. A logo that should stay in a fixed corner is a poor fit, unless you plan to move the whole set.
Avoid grouping an entire page. When everything is one group, you have to double-click to reach each part. That slows down small edits. Keep groups small and only group what you truly move together.
Keyboard shortcuts for Canva on Mac

Mac shortcuts use four modifier keys. Command is ⌘, Shift is ⇧, Option is ⌥ and Control is ⌃. Apple lists these symbols in its keyboard guide. Group and ungroup use Command, with Shift added for ungroup.

Browser shortcuts can clash with Canva's own shortcuts. Jennifer Maker warns about this and suggests trying another browser or the Canva desktop app. If Command+G seems to do nothing in the browser, test it in the desktop app.
Which version of Canva this guide covers

Canva's own help pages returned errors while this guide was written, so the steps come from third-party guides. The most recent Mac build found in the sources is Canva 1.126.2, released Oct 21, 2026, according to Uptodown. A search snippet also gave 1.126.0 from Sept 18, 2026. Neither number is confirmed by Canva.
The sources show no difference in the grouping steps between the browser and the desktop app. If a label on your screen differs, pick the nearest match and test with a scrap design first.
Mistakes people make when grouping
The first mistake is pressing Ctrl+G on a Mac. Use Command instead. The second is grouping too early. Group after you arrange things, so you do not have to ungroup and regroup later.

The third mistake is missing a hidden element inside a drag box. Zoom out and check the selection outline. The fourth is forgetting that a grouped element is still part of a group. Click one part of a group and you may select the whole group. Double-click to reach a single element.
A worked example: grouping a flyer

Say you are making a flyer for a community event. It has a headline, a subhead, a photo, a shape behind the text, and a logo in the corner. You want the headline, subhead and shape to move together. The photo and logo should stay separate.

Zoom out so the whole flyer fits. Drag a box around the headline, subhead and shape only, starting on an empty part of the canvas. Check that the outline covers only those three. Press Command+G, then drag the group to test its position.
Now check the stack. The photo may sit higher than the shape, and grouping can reorder layers. If the shape moves above the photo, fix the order before you finish.
Finally, double-click the subhead to edit it. The photo and logo stay outside the group, so you can move them on their own.
Can you group elements on the free plan?

MakeUseOf says selecting and grouping work in Canva's free version. That helps if you want to test a layout before you pay. This guide did not check Canva's pricing page, so check their pricing page before you rely on this for paid work.
Why the Group button is greyed out
A greyed-out Group button means Canva does not see a valid group. The causes below come from search summaries and third-party guides. Canva's help pages were not available to confirm them.

items: One of the selected elements is locked.
The selection includes content from the Apps tab.
You are still typing inside a text box.
The selected elements sit on different pages.

blocks.text: Work through that list in order. Select a second element. Turn off the lock on anything locked. Click out of the text box. Keep the selection on one page. Then press Command+G again.
Check that Canva is up to date on your Mac

The update path depends on how you installed Canva. If you got it from the Mac App Store, open the App Store, go to the Updates tab, and update it there. GeeksforGeeks, last updated in October 2024, describes this path.

If you installed Canva from the website, click Canva in the top menu bar and choose Check for Updates. That item appears only when an update is available. Uptodown, a third-party download site, lists Canva 1.126.2 for Mac, released Oct 21, 2026. Canva has not confirmed that number, so treat it as a reference, not a guarantee.
Grouping on the Canva mobile app

Phone and tablet steps differ from the Mac steps. MakeUseOf describes tapping an element, tapping the three-dot button, choosing More, then Select Multiple. You tap the other elements, then tap Group under More.
If you are on a Mac, skip those steps. Use the floating toolbar, Command+G or the right-click menu from this guide.
Next steps after you group

Once the layout works, you may want to copy it. [Duplicate a design in Canva on Mac](/how-to/duplicate-a-design-in-canva) shows two ways to do that. If the desktop app acts up after a big layout change, [reset it without losing designs](/how-to/reset-the-desktop-app-in-canva).
Group the elements you move together. Leave the rest loose. Ungroup when the structure changes.

faq.question: What is the shortcut to group elements in Canva on Mac?
faq.answer: Select two or more elements, then press Command+G (⌘G). Ctrl+G is the Windows version of the shortcut, so it is the wrong key on a Mac. To ungroup, press Shift+Command+G.

faq.question: How do I ungroup elements in Canva on Mac?
faq.answer: Select the group and press Shift+Command+G. You can also choose Ungroup from the floating toolbar, or right-click the group and choose Ungroup.

faq.question: Can I group elements on the free plan?
faq.answer: MakeUseOf says selecting and grouping work in the free version of Canva. This guide did not check Canva's pricing page, so check their pricing page before you rely on that for paid work.

faq.question: Why is the Group button greyed out in Canva?
faq.answer: Third-party guides name a single selected element, a locked element, content on the Apps tab, text-edit mode, and elements on different pages as causes. Work through the troubleshooting list, then try Command+G again.

faq.question: Can I edit one element inside a group without ungrouping?
faq.answer: Yes. Double-click the element. The sources describe this for the browser version and show no difference for the Mac app, but Canva's desktop help page was not available to check.

faq.question: How do I check for a Canva update on Mac?
faq.answer: If you installed Canva from the website, click Canva in the top menu bar and choose Check for Updates. That item appears only when an update is available. If you installed it from the Mac App Store, use the Updates tab there.

appliesTo: Canva on macOS, desktop app and browser, as described by the sources
requirements: A Mac with Canva, either the desktop app or Canva open in a browser
A design with at least two elements on the page

steps.name: Open the design
steps.text: Open the design in Canva on your Mac, in the desktop app or the browser. The sources describe the browser version and show no difference for the Mac app.
steps.tip: Zoom out first if the elements are spread across the page.

steps.name: Select the first element
steps.text: Click the first element you want to group. Its selection outline appears on the canvas.

steps.name: Add the other elements
steps.text: Hold Shift and click each element you want to add. Or draw a box around them on an empty part of the canvas to select them all at once.

steps.name: Group with Command+G
steps.text: Press Command+G. Canva groups the selected elements into one group.
steps.tip: On a Mac, do not use Ctrl+G. That is the Windows shortcut.

steps.name: Or use the floating toolbar
steps.text: Look for the floating toolbar near the selection. With two or more elements selected, it shows a Group button. Click Group.

steps.name: Or use the right-click menu
steps.text: Right-click one of the selected elements and choose Group.

steps.name: Test the group
steps.text: Drag the group to a new spot. Check that the elements move together before you keep working.
steps.tip: If the Group button is missing, see the troubleshooting list.

steps.name: Edit one element without ungrouping
steps.text: Double-click the element inside the group. Change the text or content, then click outside the element.

steps.name: Ungroup when you need to
steps.text: Select the group, then press Shift+Command+G. You can also choose Ungroup from the floating toolbar or from the right-click menu on the group.

troubleshooting.fix: Select at least two elements. Turn off the lock on any locked element in the selection, then try again. Third-party guides name these as the usual causes.

troubleshooting.problem: No Group button in the toolbar
troubleshooting.fix: Click out of any text box you are editing, then select the elements again. Third-party guides say text-edit mode can stop grouping.

troubleshooting.problem: Group stays greyed out across pages
troubleshooting.fix: Some guides name elements on different pages as the cause. Select elements from one page at a time, then try again.

troubleshooting.problem: Ctrl+G does nothing on a Mac
troubleshooting.fix: Use Command+G. Ctrl+G is the Windows shortcut for grouping.
That item appears only when an update is available, and only if you installed Canva from the website. If you installed it from the Mac App Store, use the Updates tab instead.

troubleshooting.problem: Cannot edit text inside a group
troubleshooting.fix: Double-click the element itself. It stays in the group after you edit it.
